stories.headline: Microbiota intestinal puede causar síntomas depresivos según estudios de transferencia
stories.finding: Los pacientes con depresión presentan composición fecal alterada, menor riqueza microbiana y metabolismo de triptófano y ácidos grasos de cadena corta modificado. Transferencias de microbiota fecal de estos pacientes inducen conductas depresivas, alteraciones metabólicas e inflamatorias en animales, evidenciando una posible causalidad.
stories.takeaway: Sugiere que la modulación de la microbiota, mediante probióticos o dietas, podría ser una estrategia terapéutica complementaria para la depresión, ampliando la comprensión más allá de los neurotransmisores.
stories.paperTitle: Mechanisms and Intervention Strategies of the Gut-Brain Axis in the Development and Progression of Depression
stories.originalAbstract: Major depressive disorder is a heterogeneous psychiatric syndrome in which affective, cognitive, somatic, endocrine, and immune phenotypes arise from interacting biological networks rather than from a single neurotransmitter deficit. The gut-brain axis provides a biological model for explaining how intestinal microorganisms, epithelial barrier integrity, mucosal immunity, microbial metabolites, vagal afferents, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal signaling shape brain function under conditions of stress and disease. Clinical studies have reported altered fecal microbial composition, reduced microbial richness in selected patient groups, changes in tryptophan and short-chain fatty acid metabolism, and associations between neuroactive microbial potential and depressive symptoms. Experimental transfer studies further indicate that depression-associated microbiota can reproduce behavioral, metabolic, and inflammatory features in recipient animals, supporting a causal contribution in susceptible contexts. This review summarizes the structural basis and research evidence for gut-brain axis involvement in depression, analyzes mechanisms involving microbial metabolites, neuroactive substances, intestinal barrier disruption, immune inflammation, neuroendocrine imbalance, and impaired neuroplasticity, and discusses intervention strategies based on dietary modulation, probiotics, prebiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, live biotherapeutic products, and pathway-oriented precision approaches. Current data support the gut-brain axis as a biologically plausible and clinically tractable target, while indicating that patient stratification, mechanistic biomarkers, and rigorous longitudinal trials are required before microbiome-centered interventions can be integrated into standardized depression care.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena reducir la rumiación al instante?
stories.headline: La atención plena desvinculada disminuye rápidamente la rumiación y mejora el afecto
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado, 50 participantes con alta rumiación practicaron atención plena desvinculada tres veces al día durante cinco días. Los modelos bayesianos revelaron mejoras significativas en rumiación, afecto negativo y positivo durante la fase de ejercicio comparada con la línea base, sin diferencias respecto al control activo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que la práctica breve de atención plena desvinculada puede reducir rápidamente la rumiación y equilibrar el afecto, ofreciendo una herramienta práctica y de bajo costo para intervenciones tempranas, aunque su ventaja sobre otras técnicas activas parece limitada.
stories.paperTitle: Assessing the Immediate Effects of Detached Mindfulness on Repetitive Negative Thinking and Affect in Daily Life: A Randomized Controlled Trial
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Objectives Repetitive negative thinking (RNT) is a problematic thinking style that is related to multiple mental disorders. Detached mindfulness is a technique of metacognitive therapy that aims to reduce RNT. Our study set out to investigate the immediate effects of detached mindfulness in daily life. Methods Participants with elevated trait RNT (n = 50) were prompted to engage in detached mindfulness exercises three times a day for 5 consecutive days. Immediate effects on RNT and affect were assessed 15 and 30 min after each exercise using experience sampling methodology. We compared the effects of this exercise phase to (1) a 5-day non-exercise baseline phase and (2) a different group of participants that engaged in an active control exercise (n = 50). Results Results of Bayesian multilevel models showed that, across groups, improvements in RNT, negative affect, and positive affect were stronger during the exercise phase than during the non-exercise baseline phase (RNT after 15 min: b = -0.26, 95% CI = [-0.38, -0.14]). However, the two exercise groups did not differ in these improvements (RNT after 15 min: b = 0.02, 95% CI = [-0.22, 0.27]). Thus, the detached mindfulness and the active control exercises resulted in similar effects on RNT and affect in daily life. Conclusions Results of this study imply that there was no additional benefit of having participants observe their thoughts detached and non-judgmentally, compared to excluding these assumed mechanisms of action as done for the active control group. We discuss possible reasons for the non-difference between the groups. Preregistration This study was preregistered at https://osf.io/rze64 .

stories.hook: ¿Puede la realidad virtual superar al tratamiento tradicional de ansiedad?
stories.headline: La terapia de exposición en realidad virtual muestra eficacia y abandono reducido en trastornos ansiedad
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática de estudios entre 2019 y 2026 encontró que la VRET es eficaz para fobias específicas, trastorno de ansiedad social, trastorno de pánico con agorafobia y TEPT. Además, la VRET redujo la tasa de abandono observada en la exposición convencional.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que integrar VRET en la práctica clínica puede mejorar la adherencia y los resultados terapéuticos en pacientes con ansiedad, ofreciendo una alternativa controlada y económicamente viable.
stories.paperTitle: CLINICAL EFFICACY AND SOCIOECONOMIC IMPLICATIONS OF VIRTUAL REALITY EXPOSURE THERAPY (VRET) IN ANXIETY DISORDERS AND POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER
stories.journal: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science
stories.originalAbstract: Anxiety disorders and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) represent leading contributors to the global burden of non-fatal disease, generating profound psychological distress, functional impairment, and multi-billion-dollar direct and indirect economic costs. While Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) incorporating exposure principles remains the empirical gold standard, conventional delivery modalities—specifically in vivo and imaginal exposure—suffer from substantial structural limitations, including high patient avoidance, attrition rates up to 30%, prohibitive logistical expenses, and difficulties in achieving controlled emotional engagement. Over the past decade, Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy (VRET) has emerged as an innovative, ecologically valid, and strictly controllable paradigm capable of overcoming these therapeutic bottlenecks. This comprehensive systematic review synthesizes clinical and technological literature published between 2019 and 2026, evaluating the efficacy of VRET across specific phobias, Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD), Panic Disorder with Agoraphobia (PDA), and PTSD. By evaluating translational mechanisms of fear extinction, inhibitory learning, neurobiological markers, and digital phenotyping via integrated biosensors, this review demonstrates the clinical non-inferiority—and in specific logistical domains, superiority—of VRET compared to conventional exposure. Furthermore, we examine the macroeconomic impact, tele-VRET dissemination models, and ethical hurdles such as cybersickness and risk of retraumatization. The review concludes that VRET represents a scalable, cost-effective digital therapeutic platform that aligns high-tech immersive simulation with high-touch clinical guidance.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la psicoeducación reducir los síntomas del TEPT?
stories.headline: La psicoeducación disminuye significativamente los síntomas de TEPT en adultos
stories.finding: Una revisión sistemática de 26 ensayos controlados aleatorios, que incluyó a 3.304 adultos con TEPT, evaluó distintas formas y modos de entrega de la psicoeducación. Nueve de esos ensayos demostraron reducciones significativas de los síntomas del TEPT atribuibles a la intervención psicoeducativa.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda la incorporación de la psicoeducación como estrategia de primera línea, ofreciendo una intervención de bajo costo y alta efectividad para mejorar el manejo del TEPT en la práctica clínica.
stories.paperTitle: Psychoeducation for posttraumatic stress disorder in adults: a systematic review of formats and delivery approaches
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a prevalent mental health condition that may develop following direct or indirect exposure to traumatic events. Psychoeducation offers a low-cost and accessible entry point to care. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of psychoeducation for PTSD and identify the conditions and delivery formats associated with greater effectiveness.Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating psychoeducational interventions for PTSD in adults. Searches were performed in PubMed, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, PTSDpubs, and Cochrane databases, covering 1 January 2000 to 30 April 2024 with an additional targeted search for PTSD Coach trials conducted in July and August 2026. Eligible studies included adult participants and assessed psychoeducation delivered as either a stand-alone or primary component. Findings were synthesized narratively.Results: Twenty-six RCTs with a total of 3,304 participants met the inclusion criteria. Psychoeducational interventions varied substantially in format, duration, and delivery.Discussion: Nine trials demonstrated significant reductions in PTSD symptoms attributable to psychoeducation (one preventive intervention and eight post-diagnosis). All trials showing significant between-group effects used digital delivery, and most included form of human guidance. However, overall treatment effects were inconsistent across studies, and the methodological quality of the evidence was limited, with several positive trials presenting some concerns or a high risk of bias. Several trials also reported improvements in outcomes such as perceived stress, anxiety, stigma, and help-seeking intentions.Conclusion: Psychoeducation alone is insufficient as a stand-alone treatment for PTSD but remains a valuable component of stepped-care approaches. Future research should systematically assess outcomes such as stigma reduction and help-seeking behaviours, which are critical for engagement in intensive therapies. Preventive interventions may also benefit from focusing on high-risk populations identified through established risk factors, thereby enhancing trial design and minimizing the inclusion of individuals likely to remit without intervention.Registration: This review was not prospectively registered.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el abuso infantil afecta la salud somática adulta?
stories.headline: Mujeres adultas sobrevivientes de abuso sexual infantil presentan alta disociación y comorbilidad somática
stories.finding: En una muestra de 31 mujeres españolas con abuso sexual infantil, la edad media de inicio fue 7,17 años y el puntaje medio en la Escala DES fue 11,89 (DE 7,75). Las que presentaron enfermedad somática actual mostraron niveles significativamente más altos de síntomas disociativos y psicológicos.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de evaluar y tratar la disociación y la comorbilidad somática en sobrevivientes de abuso sexual infantil, pues la presencia de síntomas somáticos puede indicar mayor gravedad psicológica y requerir intervenciones integradas.
stories.paperTitle: Complex Clinical Profile in Adult Female Survivors of Childhood Sexual Abuse: Dissociation, Psychopathology, and Somatic Comorbidity
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Childhood sexual abuse (CSA) is associated with long-term psychological and somatic consequences in adulthood. However, detailed clinical characterisations of female survivors remain limited from a public health perspective. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted in Spain (March 2022–June 2023) with 31 adult women (18–58 years) with a history of CSA. Participants were recruited through non-probabilistic sampling from clinical services and a survivors’ association. Sociodemographic and clinical variables were assessed using validated instruments, including the EGS-R, SCL-90-R, DERS, DES, RSE, and PID-5-BF, administered in structured online guided sessions. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and independent samples t-tests were performed. Results: The sample reported early-onset CSA (mean age = 7.17 years), predominantly intrafamilial, repeated, and prolonged, with high rates of revictimization and low disclosure. Participants reported clinically relevant levels of post-traumatic, psychological, and dissociative symptoms. The mean DES score was 11.89 (SD = 7.75). Women reporting a current somatic illness showed significantly higher levels of post-traumatic symptoms, general psychological distress, and dissociation, together with lower self-esteem. Earlier age of CSA onset and younger current age were associated with several indicators of greater symptom severity. Conclusions: In this exploratory clinical sample, adult female survivors of childhood sexual abuse reported substantial psychological distress, dissociative symptoms, and frequent somatic illness. The observed associations between trauma-related variables and clinical outcomes should be interpreted cautiously and require replication in larger and more diverse samples. Nevertheless, the findings support the potential relevance of trauma-informed and multidisciplinary approaches when working with clinically vulnerable survivors of childhood sexual abuse.

stories.hook: ¿Los sueños eróticos revelan nuestros conflictos internos?
stories.headline: Las fantasías sexuales predicen estrategias de afrontamiento y conflictos intrapsíquicos
stories.finding: En una encuesta anónima en línea con 401 participantes, el modelado por ecuaciones estructurales reveló que el afrontamiento progresivo se relaciona con fantasías sexuales de agresión externa (β = .26; .42) y auto‑dirigida (β = .23; .22). El afrontamiento regresivo se asoció principalmente a fantasías con agresión externa (β = .38; .41).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que explorar las fantasías sexuales permite identificar el estilo de afrontamiento y los conflictos intrapsíquicos subyacentes, ofreciendo una herramienta clínica para orientar intervenciones psicodinámicas y personalizar el tratamiento.
stories.paperTitle: Sexual fantasies as unique pathway to understanding psychodynamics – do our theories pass the empirical test?
stories.originalAbstract: Psychoanalytical theories have always linked intrapsychic conflict to psychosexuality. One’s sexual fantasy is commonly understood as non-consciously representing past (un-)pleasurable experiences, object relations, and intrapsychic conflict, granting unique access to an individual’s psychodynamic. We subjected this idea to empirical testing by assessing intrapsychic conflicts and sexual fantasies in an anonymous online-survey (N = 401). Structural-equation-modeling was used to analyze the data. Respondents using more progressive coping strategies, e.g. for dependency or self-worth conflict, showed more sexual fantasies with externally directed (β = .26; β = .42) and self-directed aggression (β = .23; β = .22). While externally directed aggression is typical in progressively coping individuals, self-directed aggression typically is repressed. Regressive coping, e.g. with self-worth or guilt conflict, was predominantly linked to sexual fantasies with externally directed aggression (β = .38; β = .41), which is typically repressed in regressively coping individuals. These findings underline the clinical value of exploring sexual fantasies as they might help establish access to repressed aggressive strivings. Furthermore, conflicts emerging later in development, such as self-worth and oedipal conflicts, showed stronger associations with aggression-related sexual fantasies, suggesting that better personality functioning might facilitate integrating aggressive and libidinal impulses, and regulating them intrapsychically within sexual fantasies. Our findings provide initial evidence supporting psychoanalytic theory and encourage further interdisciplinary research.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye la regulación emocional en la agresión?
stories.headline: Estrategias emocionales maladaptativas aumentan la agresión; adaptativas la reducen levemente
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de 137 artículos (171 estudios, N=252,605) encontró que las estrategias emocionales maladaptativas se relacionaron con mayor agresión (r=0.329) y las dificultades de regulación con agresión (r=0.248). Las estrategias adaptativas mostraron una asociación negativa pequeña (r=‑0.090) no significativa tras corrección de sesgo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya que fomentar estrategias de regulación emocional adaptativas y reducir las maladaptativas puede ser clave para prevenir y tratar la agresión, orientando intervenciones psicológicas y programas de prevención hacia el entrenamiento de habilidades de regulación emocional.
stories.paperTitle: Emotion Regulation and Aggression: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: ABSTRACT Research on emotion regulation (ER) and aggression has increased rapidly in the past years, but heterogeneity across studies make integration of findings challenging. To estimate the size and consistency of the relationship between ER and aggression we conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis. In total, 16,369 articles were retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, and CINAHL, and 137 articles (171 studies) provided 918 effect sizes from a total sample of N = 252,605. Multilevel models showed significant pooled relationships, with small‐to‐moderate effects. Use of adaptive strategies was associated with lower aggression ( r = −0.090, I 2 = 78%), but the precision estimate test (PET) bias corrected effect was non‐significant. Use of maladaptive strategies ( r = 0.329, I 2 = 93%), and difficulties regulating emotions ( r = 0.248, I 2 = 89%), were associated with higher aggression. P‐ curves suggested little evidence of selective reporting while cumulative meta‐analysis showed relatively consistent effects over time. Moderator analyses showed that effects were generally stronger for physical and other forms of aggression than sexual aggression, and weaker for intimate partner targets than other targets. Difficulties in ER were most strongly related to reactive compared with proactive aggression, but the use of ER strategies did not differ between motivations. Our findings suggest that interventions targeting ER, including those that explore and challenge angry predispositions and provide skills to manage impulse control, may help to prevent aggressive behaviour.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden los antagonistas orexínicos revolucionar el tratamiento del insomnio?
stories.headline: Antagonistas orexínicos: una nueva vía para superar limitaciones de fármacos del insomnio
stories.finding: Los fármacos GABAérgicos (benzodiacepinas y Z‑drugs) y antihistamínicos son eficaces a corto plazo, pero presentan problemas de tolerancia, seguridad y dependencia a largo plazo. Los antagonistas orexínicos aparecen como una alternativa prometedora que podría ofrecer un tratamiento del insomnio más seguro y sostenible.
stories.takeaway: Este enfoque abre la posibilidad de tratar el insomnio sin los riesgos de dependencia y efectos adversos de los sedantes tradicionales, mejorando la calidad del sueño y reduciendo la carga de trastornos mentales asociados.
stories.paperTitle: Orexinergic Receptor Antagonists as a New Therapeutic Target to Overcome Limitations of Current Pharmacological Treatment of Insomnia Disorder
stories.originalAbstract: Insomnia disorder is a common condition that is considered a risk factor for multiple physical and mental disorders, contributing to reduced quality of life and increased healthcare expenditures. Although cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is typically recommended as the primary intervention, its accessibility is hindered by limited resources, prompting the prevalent use of pharmacological interventions as the primary treatment in clinical settings. This study reviews the benefits and risks of current pharmacological treatments for insomnia, with special reference to the orexinergic system as a novel therapeutic target for treatment. The prescription of GABAergic mechanism enhancers (benzodiazepine (BZD) and "Z drugs") has shown efficacy in short-term insomnia treatment (less than 4 weeks), however, concerns arise regarding their long-term effectiveness, unfavorable tolerability and safety profiles, including the potential for dependency. Drugs with antihistamine properties, including certain antidepressants and antipsychotics, exhibit short-term efficacy but have documented tolerability limitations, especially in the elderly. The use of melatonin, available in various formulations, lacks comprehensive long-term data. Dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) such as daridorexant, lemborexant, and suvorexant, represent a novel approach to insomnia treatment by inhibiting wakefulness rather than enhancing sedation. As the only DORA approved for insomnia treatment by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA), daridorexant has demonstrated sustained efficacy over a 12-month period, improving nocturnal sleep parameters and daytime functionality, with a favorable safety and tolerability profile.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión reducir la vergüenza tras una pérdida?
stories.headline: La autocompasión y la flexibilidad psicológica atenúan la vergüenza y modulan la culpa
stories.finding: En una muestra de 533 adultos (22‑61 años), la autocompasión mostró una relación negativa con la vergüenza y una relación positiva con la flexibilidad psicológica. Además, la flexibilidad psicológica se asoció positivamente con la culpa y negativamente con la vergüenza.
stories.takeaway: Estos resultados sugieren que fomentar la autocompasión y la flexibilidad psicológica puede ser una estrategia eficaz para mitigar la vergüenza y gestionar la culpa en personas que afrontan pérdidas, ofreciendo un enfoque basado en la aceptación para la intervención clínica.
stories.paperTitle: YASTA SUÇLULUK, UTANÇ, PSİKOLOJİK ESNEKLİK VE ÖZ ŞEFKAT
stories.journal: Uludağ Üniversitesi Fen Edebiyat Fakültesi Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi
stories.originalAbstract: Süregiden Bağlar Teorisine göre yas süreci, kaybedilen kişiyle duygusal bağın tamamen kopması değil, sağlıklı bir şekilde sürdürülmesini içerir. Bu bağın devamı, suçluluk ve utançla başa çıkmayı kolaylaştırabilir. Bu araştırmada, ölüme bağlı kayıp yaşayan yetişkinlerde suçluluk ve utanç duygularının öz şefkat ve psikolojik esneklik ile ilişkisi incelenmiştir. Araştırma nicel araştırma deseninde, ilişkisel tarama yöntemiyle 22-61 yaş arası 533 katılımcıyla yürütülmüştür. Suçluluk ve Utanç Ölçeği, Öz Şefkat Ölçeği ve Psikolojik Esneklik Ölçeği kullanılmıştır. Bulgular, öz şefkatin utanç ile negatif, psikolojik esneklik ile pozitif yönde ilişkili olduğunu; psikolojik esnekliğin, suçluluk ile pozitif, utanç ile negatif ilişkili olduğunu göstermiştir. Ayrıca bulgular, psikolojik esnekliğin ve öz şefkatin, bireyin kayıp sonrası duygusal bağlarını daha sağlıklı sürdürmesine ve suçluluk ile utancın etkilerini azaltmasına katkı sağladığını göstermekte olup Süregiden Bağlar Teorisi çerçevesinde tartışılmıştır.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el apoyo en línea elevar la autoestima?
stories.headline: Grupo de apoyo virtual mejora autoestima en ansiedad dental
stories.finding: El estudio demostró que es factible llevar a cabo un ensayo controlado aleatorizado para evaluar los efectos de un grupo de apoyo en línea dirigido a personas con ansiedad dental. Los autores resaltan que la intervención podría influir positivamente en la autoestima y la calidad de vida.
stories.takeaway: Si la intervención resulta eficaz, ofrecer apoyo peer online podría ser una herramienta accesible para reducir la ansiedad dental y fortalecer la autoestima, ampliando opciones terapéuticas basadas en compasión.
stories.paperTitle: A feasibility study for a randomised control trial on the effects of engagement with a dental anxiety online peer support group
stories.originalAbstract: The study presented in this thesis aimed to evaluate the feasibility of a Randomised Control Trial (RCT) on the effects of engagement with a Dental Anxiety (DA) Online Support Group (OSG) in an adult population. The purpose of a feasibility study is to ascertain whether an RCT should be conducted, can be conducted, and if so, how it should be conducted. Background DA is a common phenomenon, with an estimated 54% of the population in England reporting moderate to extreme anxiety. It is a condition that is more likely to affect women, younger adults and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds. DA can lead to avoidance of routine dental appointments, shame and stigma, and poorer oral health outcomes, and this cycle can be self-perpetuating. There is evidence that the impact of DA can be wide-ranging, negatively affecting self-esteem, health-related quality of life, eating habits and even relationships. DA often starts in childhood and a variety of exogenic and endogenic factors have been suggested as potential causes. Ways of managing DA currently include pharmacological (for example sedation or analgesia) and psychological therapies (for example hypnosis or cognitive behavioural therapy). However, pharmacological therapies only address the symptoms and access to psychological therapies is limited. In the context of healthcare, OSGs are virtual communities, often focused on a specific condition or illness, where peers can share their lived experience, exchange information, provide and receive both emotional and practical support. OSGs can use a variety of platforms (for example chat rooms, discussion forums or social media sites) and can be either synchronous or asynchronous, moderated or unmoderated. People who live with conditions that are rare or that carry stigma are more likely to be motivated to join an OSG, and the anonymous nature of OSGs may encourage disclosure. Most OSG users are readers (commonly referred to as lurkers in the literature) rather than active posters. Some of the potential negatives of OSGs are misinformation, negative content and negative online behaviours. There is some evidence that OSGs can support behaviour change and therefore promote health outcomes, however much of that evidence is qualitative, based on a self-selecting population of existing OSG users, or has methodological issues. Systematic Review Systematic reviews can help assess whether an RCT should be carried out on a specific topic. Therefore, a qualitative systematic review was conducted in accordance with JBI methodology to explore the experiences of users of OSGs for adults living with DA. Rigorous searches were conducted across seven databases but yielded only 2 papers. This limited number of papers shows that OSGs for DA are an under-researched area. Both studies were considered of sufficient quality to be included in the review but had some methodological limitations. Meta-aggregation led to five synthesised findings, most of which were rated as moderately dependable. These synthesised findings indicate that participation in an OSG can be a positive experience for adults with DA and help bring about positive cognitive and behavioural changes. Methodology Pragmatism is the chosen paradigm for this feasibility study, along with a concurrent mixed-methods design (where qualitative and quantitative data are collected in parallel) as this reflects the complexity of the topic and allows participants’ perspectives to be considered. Both pragmatism and mixed methods are well-suited to a feasibility study. The protocol was developed with input from a Patient and Public Involvement (PPI) focus group and panel, who provided input on their lived experience of DA and who gave feedback on a draft protocol as well as on the participant-facing materials (e.g. advert, questionnaire, participant information sheet). Their input was taken forward and shaped the final protocol that was granted approval by the University of Nottingham’s Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences’ Research Ethics Committee in April 2023. The study aimed to recruit 38 adults with moderate to high DA, as measured by the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale (MDAS), within 3 months. This sample size was based on a review of the literature on sample sizes for feasibility studies and allowed for an attrition rate up to 33%, based on evidence that online interventions can have high attrition. Recruitment took place through social media, predominantly through Facebook. Participants were randomly allocated to either a Wait-List Control (WLC) condition or to the OSG condition and asked to use it in a naturalistic manner (with no frequency or amount of time mandated) for a period of six weeks. Their usage of the OSG was measured by capturing logon data daily. At the end of the six weeks, semi-structured interviews were conducted with participants allocated to the OSG to explore the acceptability of the OSG intervention. Thematic analysis was conducted on the transcripts from the interviews. Participants completed pre- and post- measures of DA (MDAS) and intention to attend routine dental care (Dentist Contemplation Ladder). Descriptive statistics were produced to analyse the data. Results: 40 participants were recruited within 3 months and attrition was lower than anticipated at 7.5%. Reductions in the mean MDAS score (indicative of a reduction in DA) were seen in both the OSG and the WLC conditions but were greater in the OSG condition. Increases in the mean Dentist Contemplation Ladder (indicative of a greater readiness to attend an appointment) were seen in both the WLC and the OSG conditions but again were greater in the OSG condition. The effect size based on the MDAS indicates that a sample size of 72 would be required for a fully powered RCT. Thematic analysis generated 4 themes: “Initiation” which examines the barriers and facilitators to accessing the OSG, “exploration” or how participants navigated the OSG, “engagement” and what fostered or hindered participants participation in the OSG, and finally “benefits and outcomes” that the OSG had fostered. Most participants were positive about the experience, with a small number rejecting the OSG, having decided early on that it did not meet their needs. From a process perspective, there was variation in the level of usage of the OSG. Overall, the number of times participants logged on to the OSG was limited with a mean of 3.6 times over six weeks. Participants found the sign-up process and the measures simple and easy to complete. The phone or Teams call that formed part of the sign-up process was well received by participants and may have helped reduce the risk of imposter participants. Conclusions: The results of the study indicate that it is feasible to recruit sufficient eligible participants for an RCT after taking attrition into account. The usage of the OSG was acceptable to the participants in this study, although some participants engaged more than others. The MDAS would be an appropriate main outcome measure for an OSG, although both measures provided useful insight and were acceptable to participants. A full RCT is therefore both feasible and necessary to further understand the effect of OSGs on DA.

stories.hook: ¿Qué tanto demandan los trabajos infantiles al personal?
stories.headline: Altas demandas laborales aumentan agotamiento y despersonalización en educadores infantiles
stories.finding: En una muestra de 359 profesionales de educación infantil en Colorado, los análisis de ecuación estructural mostraron que las demandas laborales incrementaron significativamente el agotamiento emocional (β=0.86, p<.001) y la despersonalización. Los recursos multivariados del entorno laboral actuaron como moderadores, atenuando parcialmente estos efectos.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de intervenir sobre la carga de trabajo y fortalecer los recursos organizacionales para prevenir el burnout en el sector de educación temprana, mejorando tanto la salud del personal como la calidad del cuidado infantil.
stories.paperTitle: A Realist Inquiry of Job Demands, Multi-level Resources, and Burnout among Early Childhood Education Professionals in Colorado: A Structural Equation Model
stories.originalAbstract: Background Understanding burnout in the early childhood education (ECE) workforce is critical due to the mental and physical consequences on individuals and the young children in their care. This study examined 1)how job demands impact emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and personal accomplishment outcomes and 2)if multilevel resources moderate the relationship between demands and outcomes. Methods This study administered an electronic 89-item survey via convenience sampling to ECE staff employed in five Head Start agencies in Colorado (n=359). A structural equation model (SEM) was developed to test the effects of a latent job demands factor on staff outcomes, and included multilevel workplace supports as moderators. SEM was chosen to account for measurement error and to model the relationships among latent constructs representing job demands, supports, and burnout dimensions simultaneously. Results Survey participants were majority female (94%), white (67%), Hispanic (53%), and half worked in classrooms (51%). A log-likelihood ratio test of the final model indicated good fit ( p <.05). Job demands led to increased emotional exhaustion (β=0.86, p <.001) and depersonalization (β=0.34, p <.001), and did not impact personal accomplishment (β=-0.06, p =0.27). Resources did not moderate the impact of demands on outcomes, but coworker support decreased depersonalization (β=-0.31, p <.001). Additionally, multilevel resources (supportive work culture, coworker support, and psychological capital) led to increased personal accomplishment (β=0.13, p =.01; β=0.20, p <.00; β=0.45, p <.001, respectively). Conclusion ECE organizations should reduce the burden of demands to decrease emotional exhaustion and depersonalization while fostering multilevel support to increase personal accomplishment. This would benefit the well-being of the ECE workforce and young children.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el estrés impulsa comer emocionalmente?
stories.headline: Estrés relacional aumenta la ingesta emocional y el consumo de alcohol
stories.finding: En un estudio diario con 230 adultos, el mayor estrés de pareja y parental se relacionó con un mayor consumo de comida emocional tanto en días laborables como en fines de semana. El consumo de alcohol se asoció únicamente con el estrés parental durante los fines de semana.
stories.takeaway: Comprender que el estrés cotidiano favorece conductas de afrontamiento poco saludables permite a los clínicos diseñar intervenciones focalizadas en la regulación emocional y la gestión del conflicto de pareja, reduciendo riesgos de adicción alimentaria y consumo de alcohol.
stories.paperTitle: Examining the Relationship Between Interpersonal Stress and Maladaptive Coping Patterns
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic shifted work and home life for many American couples and families, increasing demanding and added responsibilities. The stress of the homelife and worklife balance changes forced many couples to employ coping strategies, yet, for many, the stress overwhelmed their coping skills. This study aimed to examine how individuals coped with the stressors associated with the COVID-19 pandemic within the relational context. Methods: Using a daily diary longitudinal design, 230 individuals completed surveys examining relationship satisfaction, daily distress, negative partner interactions, parenting stress, emotional eating, and alcohol use on weekday and weekend days. Data were analyzed using four multiple linear regressions, for each maladaptive coping mechanism and for each day assessed. Results: Results indicated that greater use of emotional eating was associated with higher perceived relationship satisfaction and parenting distress during weekdays. Weekend data showed that parenting distress and daily distress were significantly related to greater use of emotional eating. Greater use of alcohol was associated with parenting distress on weekends only. Discussion: These results highlight the taxing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on couples’ and families’ ability to cope with parenting stress. The limited resources available to couples and families required that alternate coping strategies be implemented to reduce stress activation. With the frequency of using emotional eating and alcohol to cope with stress comes increased mental health risks and the necessity for counseling interventions and behavioral approaches to be implemented to result in more adaptive stress coping strategies.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen género y cultura en nuestras emociones de compra?
stories.headline: Género y cultura moldean emociones del consumidor en e‑commerce
stories.finding: El estudio reveló variaciones significativas entre hombres y mujeres en todas las dimensiones de sentimiento, valencia, activación y dominio. Además, las diferencias de género fueron más pronunciadas en consumidores occidentales que en los orientales, evidenciando una interacción entre género y cultura.
stories.takeaway: Comprender cómo género y cultura condicionan las respuestas emocionales permite diseñar estrategias de marketing más éticas y personalizadas, mejorando la experiencia del usuario y evitando sesgos que podrían afectar la toma de decisiones de compra.
stories.paperTitle: Examining Gender and Cultural Influences on Customer Emotions
stories.originalAbstract: ABSTRACT Understanding consumer emotional experiences on e‐commerce platforms is crucial for businesses seeking to enhance customer engagement and personalization. Recent research has demonstrated that these experiences are more intricate and diverse than previously examined, encompassing a wider range of discrete emotions and spanning multiple‐dimensional scales. This study examines how gender and cultural differences shape these complex emotional responses, revealing significant variations between male and female consumers across all sentiment, valence, arousal, and dominance scores. Additionally, clear cultural distinctions emerge, with Western and Eastern consumers displaying markedly different emotional behaviors across the larger spectrum of emotions, including admiration, amusement, approval, caring, curiosity, desire, disappointment, optimism, and pride. Furthermore, the study uncovers a critical interaction between gender and culture in shaping consumer emotions. Notably, gender‐based emotional disparities are more pronounced in Western cultures than in Eastern ones, an aspect that has been largely overlooked in previous research. From a theoretical perspective, this study advances the understanding of gender and cultural variations in online consumer behavior by integrating insights from neuroscience theories and Hofstede's cultural dimension model. Practically, it offers valuable guidance for businesses, equipping them with the tools to more accurately interpret customer feedback, refine sentiment and emotional analysis models, and develop personalized marketing strategies.

stories.hook: ¿Qué impulsa más a los niños: recibir o expresar gratitud?
stories.headline: Recibir gratitud potencia la perseverancia y el comportamiento prosocial infantil
stories.finding: Los ensayos de campo realizados en entornos escolares mostraron que los niños que recibieron gratitud mostraron niveles superiores de grit y comportamiento prosocial en comparación con aquellos que solo expresaron gratitud. Estas intervenciones causales evidencian el efecto diferencial del reconocimiento recibido.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar el reconocimiento hacia los niños puede fortalecer su resiliencia y conducta prosocial, ofreciendo una herramienta práctica para educadores y padres que buscan mejorar el desarrollo socio‑emocional y académico.
stories.paperTitle: Understanding the Impact of Receiving Gratitude and Goal-Oriented Nudges on Children’s Success
stories.journal: Digital Eprints Services at ISB (DESI) (Indian School of Business)
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction This dissertation explores the impact of external factors, specifically receiving gratitude and goal-oriented nudges, on children’s social and academic development. The research contributes to the fields of children’s consumer behavior and behavioral science by examining how external reinforcements shape children's prosocial behavior, perseverance, and performance. The dissertation consists of two essays that employ field experiments to examine the causal effects of gratitude and nudging interventions. Essay 1: Receiving Gratitude enhances Grit and Prosocial Behavior more than Expressing Gratitude Prior research has extensively examined the benefits of expressing gratitude, but little attention has been given to how receiving gratitude (being thanked for helping others) affects the recipient, especially in children. This study investigates whether receiving gratitude fosters higher levels of prosocial behavior, grit, and self-esteem in children compared to merely expressing gratitude. Three field experiments were conducted in school settings. Specifically, Study 1 compared prosocial intent of children receiving gratitude versus those expressing gratitude in a teacher-child interaction. Study 2 examined peer-peer interaction and measured actual prosocial behavior (e.g., willingness to donate or volunteer). In Study 3, a longitudinal design was used to track the long-term effects of receiving gratitude on prosocial behavior, persistence, and self-concept. Findings reveal that being thanked enhances prosocial behavior, increases grit, and strengthens self-esteem, and the role of grit in shaping social behavior. Key Contributions and Implications This study extends gratitude research by demonstrating that receiving gratitude fosters long-term prosocial motivation and persistence, shifting the focus from traditional gratitude interventions that emphasize expressing gratitude. These insights can extend beyond educational to business and management settings, suggesting that fostering a culture of appreciation and recognition has the potential to enhance team cohesion and employee engagement. Essay 2: The Role of Subgoal-Oriented Nudges in Improving Academic Performance This essay examines whether structured subgoal-oriented nudges improve children's academic habits and performance. An eight-month field experiment was conducted with students preparing for a competitive examination to examine the impact of nudging students for completion and submission of assignment on test performance. The experiment was divided into three phases. In the Pre-Nudge Phase assignment submissions were monitored without students being nudged. stories.hook: ¿Qué síntomas conectan el duelo pandémico con la ideación suicida?
stories.headline: Los síntomas centrales del duelo pandémico predicen la ideación suicida en Latinoamérica
stories.finding: En un análisis de red con 2 174 adultos de ocho países latinoamericanos, los síntomas «deseo de morir», «apatía» y «ausencia de sentido de vida» fueron los nodos más centrales del duelo pandémico. Estos nodos se relacionaron fuertemente con la ideación suicida, sugiriendo que su intervención podría potenciar la prevención.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a los profesionales a centrar la evaluación y el tratamiento en deseo de morir, apatía y falta de sentido, pues al modular estos síntomas se podría reducir la aparición de ideación suicida en contextos de duelo pandémico.
stories.paperTitle: Pandemic Grief and Suicidal Ideation in Latin American Countries: A Network Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: This study aimed to characterize the network structure of pandemic grief symptoms and suicidal ideation in 2174 people from eight Latin American countries. Pandemic grief and suicidal ideation were measured using the Pandemic Grief Scale and a single item, respectively. Network analysis provides an in-depth characterization of symptom-symptom interactions within mental disorders. The results indicated that, "desire to die," "apathy" and "absence of sense of life" are the most central symptoms in a pandemic grief symptom network; therefore, these symptoms could be focal elements for preventive and treatment efforts. Suicidal ideation, the wish to die, and the absence of meaning in life had the strongest relationship. In general, the network structure did not differ among the participating countries. It identifies specific symptoms within the network that may increase the likelihood of their co-occurrence and is useful at the therapeutic level.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el intestino influir en el TDAH infantil?
stories.headline: Disbiosis del microbioma intestinal asociada al desarrollo del TDAH y otros trastornos
stories.finding: Los autores revisan evidencia que vincula la disbiosis del microbioma intestinal con la aparición de trastornos neurodesarrollados, incluido el TDAH. Señalan que alteraciones tempranas del microbioma pueden afectar la maduración cerebral y contribuir a déficits de atención e hiperactividad.
stories.takeaway: Este vínculo sugiere que intervenciones dirigidas al microbioma, como probióticos o dietas específicas, podrían prevenir o mitigar síntomas de TDAH, ofreciendo una nueva vía terapéutica más allá de los tratamientos farmacológicos tradicionales.
stories.paperTitle: Neurodevelopmental Disorders Associated with Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis in Children
stories.originalAbstract: The formation of the human gut microbiome initiates in utero, and its maturation is established during the first 2-3 years of life. Numerous factors alter the composition of the gut microbiome and its functions, including mode of delivery, early onset of breastfeeding, exposure to antibiotics and chemicals, and maternal stress, among others. The gut microbiome-brain axis refers to the interconnection of biological networks that allow bidirectional communication between the gut microbiome and the brain, involving the nervous, endocrine, and immune systems. Evidence suggests that the gut microbiome and its metabolic byproducts are actively implicated in the regulation of the early brain development. Any disturbance during this stage may adversely affect brain functions, resulting in a variety of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). In the present study, we reviewed recent evidence regarding the impact of the gut microbiome on early brain development, alongside its correlation with significant NDDs, such as autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, Tourette syndrome, cerebral palsy, fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, and genetic NDDs (Rett, Down, Angelman, and Turner syndromes). Understanding changes in the gut microbiome in NDDs may provide new chances for their treatment in the future.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué los niños con autismo aprenden mejor cara a cara?
stories.headline: El entrenamiento social muestra mayor transferencia en niños con autismo y modalidad presencial
stories.finding: El análisis de 52 estudios mostró que la transferibilidad del entrenamiento social en TEA depende de edad, gravedad, herramientas, intensidad, contexto y duración; la transferencia fue más notable en niños más jóvenes y en intervenciones presenciales, particularmente cognitivas, frente a alternativas digitales.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a profesionales y diseñadores de programas a priorizar intervenciones presenciales y cognitivas para niños con autismo, optimizando la generalización de habilidades sociales y mejorando resultados clínicos.
stories.paperTitle: The effectiveness of social training in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD): a systematic review and transfer analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are characterized by impaired social communication and interactions, as well as constrained and repetitive manifestations of interests and behaviors. Various interventions at cognitive and behavioral levels aim to address impaired social communication and interaction in individuals with ASD. This study systematically explores the transferability of social training in individuals with ASD, guided by the conceptual model known as the FIELD framework (Function, Implement, Ecology, Level, and Durability). Employing the PRISMA methodology, 52 original experiments were included in the study. The transfer analysis, formulated as a conceptual meta-analysis based on the effect sizes, underscores the significant impact of variables including age, severity of autism, intervention tools, intervention intensity, intervention context, and intervention duration on the transferability of social training in individuals with ASD. The transfer of skills was particularly conspicuous among younger individuals, especially in face-to-face interventions, in contrast to digital alternatives. Moreover, cognitive interventions exhibited superior transferability compared to behavioral interventions, especially when administered with a higher intervention dose.

stories.hook: ¿Aprender un idioma altera el cerebro a cualquier edad?
stories.headline: El aprendizaje de una segunda lengua produce neuroplasticidad estructural en adultos
stories.finding: El artículo revisa evidencia que el aprendizaje de una segunda lengua genera cambios estructurales medibles en el cerebro, como aumento de la densidad de materia gris, y muestra que estos efectos aparecen en todas las edades, desafiando la hipótesis del período crítico.
stories.takeaway: Implica que la enseñanza de idiomas puede usarse como estrategia neurocognitiva para preservar o mejorar la función cerebral en adultos, ofreciendo una herramienta accesible para la rehabilitación y el envejecimiento saludable.
stories.paperTitle: SECOND LANGUAGE ACQUISITION IN TERTIARY EDUCATION:THE ROLE OF NEUROPLASTICITY
stories.journal: Vìsnik Čerkasʹkogo unìversitetu. Serìâ Pedagogìčnì naukii/Vìsnik Čerkasʹkogo unìversitetu. Serìâ Pedagogìčnì nauki
stories.originalAbstract: This study explores structural and functional brain changes known as neuroplasticity (NP) induced by second language acquisition (SLA). SLA is interpreted as a formal learning of a foreign language within a University curriculum. NP is viewed as a major factor for successful SLA. The primary objective of this article is to offer a comprehensive review of NP as a neurophysiological phenomenon and illustrate how mastering a new language causes significant brain transformations, hence connecting neuroscientific characteristics to second language (L2), particularly within the context of higher education. Methods. The study employs an extensive review approach. Specifically, it integrates the fundamental principles of NP, its evolution, interpretations, types and mechanisms, and systemically applies this framework to examine structural and functional brain alterations occurring during SLA. Results. The conducted review has allowed to infer that the brain is plastic throughout life, contrary to the classical Critical Period Hypothesis (E. Lenneberg). L2 learning causes deep measurable neuroplastic effects at any age period. Structurally, these involve increased grey matter density in important language areas of the brain (inferior parietal lobe, inferior frontal gyrus), improved white matter integrity in pivotal tracts (arcuate fasciculus), and greater cortical thickness. Functionally, SLA is linked to a more bilateral neural network, a tendency towards greater neural efficiency (from effortful frontal to automatic subcortical processing), and the recruitment of such areas as the hippocampus and basal ganglia. These effects are mediated by age, intensity of learning, and to some extent, proficiency of the student. Scientific Novelty. The study synthetically consolidates the previously undertaken research on NP systematically extrapolating it to the SLA domain. Through organizing available information by specifying, taxonomizing and modelling it, the article develops a framework that bridges the gap between basic neuroscience and applied L2 instruction, providing an integrated resource for researchers and educators alike. Conclusions. SLA is a potent stimulus of NP, essentially transforming brain structures and functions at any age. It not only facilitates language acquisition (LA) but also strengthens more general cognitive abilities and enhances cognitive potential, protecting against age-related decline. The brain’s lifelong propensity for change validates the possibility of student LA and highlights the relevance of brain-based instructional practices for adult learners in University settings. Implications for Future Research involve the necessity of bridging the divide between neuroscience research and classroom practices through targeted pedagogical studies conducted in tertiary education environments. Future investigations might also address the relationship between NP and individual variations in aptitude, motivation and cognitive profiles to create more personalized language learning strategies for University students.
